newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir says overspeculation in stocks unhealthy.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir says overspeculation in stocks unhealthy.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Wednesday that "too much speculation" in the stock market is not a healthy phenomenon.

In a speech at a KLSE charity dinner, he said he also did not understand why prices of newly-listed stocks on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) should rapidly shoot up when the companies are new to the market.
"It's good to have speculation on the stock exchange, but too much speculation becomes bad," he told the gathering of stockbrokers and industry officials.
"Sometimes the price goes up without any rhyme or reason. They doubled and trebled and they go up by five, six times especially if they are new issues," he added.
He said while he would not make any presumptions on why these stocks should climb rapidly, such movements are not healthy.
"The only thing I know is that it's not a very healthy thing to have new shares to go up that much," Mahathir said.
